title: AI double standards?
author: TheGamingSpringbok
selftext:
Anyone else feel AI use has double standards?

Like its acceptable to use AI for code but not art and music. Because art and music is more 'special' or 'x' other reason given? 

Im a programmer and visual artist so I feel this is quite contradictory. Like the gaming audience is fine with AI generated code BUT not AI generated art? Even though code and art (both take effort) can both be iterated on to find a unique style or even new gameplay prototypes. 

Also it feels Indie developers face more intense public backlash, accusations of being "lazy," and even negative reviews for using AI. 

But, major AAA corporations are often given a "pass" and dont even have to diclose AI use. NetEase for example has not included an AI disclosure on their *Steam* page for *Marvel Rivals*, YET they have reportedly admitted to using AI throughout their entire production pipelines in their financial reports in 2025. 

I feel they has to be others out there that feels some levels of hypocrisy like me and has found some other example out there. 

I feel like its just a trend and culture to hate on AI right now, and i get it, i lost a job due to it ngl. BUT we have to adapt to this AI revolution right? No one has ever just stopped a revolution after all.

Any other perspectives out there?
